findings.description: The database username and password are rendered into EC2 user data and then written to a PHP configuration file on the instance. This exposes a reusable database credential through user-data/configuration retrieval paths and to processes or principals able to read the host file.

The instance explicitly sets publicly_accessible = true, causing RDS to assign a public endpoint. The displayed ingress rule is VPC-scoped, but assigning public routability unnecessarily expands the database attack surface.
The instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving the RDS storage volume and associated automated backups unencrypted at rest.

The EC2-assumable application role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Since this role is attached to the application instance, compromise of that instance enables broad account-level data access and infrastructure modification.

The database security group permits every protocol and port to 0.0.0.0/0. This removes egress network boundaries and permits arbitrary outbound communication if the database environment is compromised.

MySQL ingress is permitted from the entire VPC CIDR rather than being restricted to the application security group or other explicitly required workloads. Any workload able to obtain an address in the VPC can attempt to connect to the database on port 3306.
